                                                                                                                                                        A client for BEDbase. bedbaser provides access to the API\nat api.bedbase.org. It also includes convenience functions to\nimport BED files into GRanges objects and BEDsets into\nGRangesLists.
#> 412                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 MaAsLin2 is comprehensive R package for efficiently\ndetermining multivariable association between clinical metadata\nand microbial meta'omic features. MaAsLin2 relies on general\nlinear models to accommodate most modern epidemiological study\ndesigns, including cross-sectional and longitudinal, and offers\na variety of data exploration, normalization, and\ntransformation methods. MaAsLin2 is the next generation of\nMaAsLin.
#> 413                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Bring the power and flexibility of AnnData to the R\necosystem, allowing you to effortlessly manipulate and analyse\nyour single-cell data. This package lets you work with backed\nh5ad and zarr files, directly access various slots (e.g. X,\nobs, var), or convert the data into SingleCellExperiment and\nSeurat objects.
#> 414                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Test for univariate and bivariate spatial patterns in\nspatial omics data with single-molecule resolution. The tests\nimplemented allow for analysis of nested designs and are\nautomatically calibrated to different biological specimens.\nTests for aggregation, colocalization, gradients and vicinity\nto cell edge or centroid are provided.
#> 415                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      ramr is an R package for detection of epimutations (i.e.,\ninfrequent aberrant DNA methylation events) in large data sets\nobtained by methylation profiling using array or\nhigh-throughput methylation sequencing. In addition, package\nprovides functions to visualize found aberrantly methylated\nregions (AMRs), to generate sets of all possible regions to be\nused as reference sets for enrichment analysis, and to generate\nbiologically relevant test data sets for performance evaluation\nof AMR/DMR search algorithms.
#> 416                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Provides functionality for untargeted LC-MS metabolomics\nresearch as specified in the associated protocol article in the\n'Metabolomics Data Processing and Data Analysis—Current Best\nPractices' special issue of the Metabolites journal (2020).\nThis includes tabular data preprocessing and quality control,\nuni- and multivariate analysis as well as quality control\nvisualizations, feature-wise visualizations and results\nvisualizations. Raw data preprocessing and functionality\nrelated to biological context, such as pathway analysis, is not\nincluded.
#> 417                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         A shiny interface to the scanMiR package. The application\nenables the scanning of transcripts and custom sequences for\nmiRNA binding sites, the visualization of KdModels and binding\nresults, as well as browsing predicted repression data. In\naddition contains the IndexedFst class for fast indexed reading\nof large GenomicRanges or data.frames, and some utilities for\nfacilitating scans and identifying enriched miRNA-target pairs.
#> 418                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      IONiseR provides tools for the quality assessment of\nOxford Nanopore MinION data. It extracts summary statistics\nfrom a set of fast5 files and can be used either before or\nafter base calling.  In addition to standard summaries of the\nread-types produced, it provides a number of plots for\nvisualising metrics relative to experiment run time or\nspatially over the surface of a flowcell.
#> 419                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Provides means to interactively visualize guide RNAs\n(gRNAs) in GuideSet objects via Shiny application. This GUI can\nbe self-contained or as a module within a larger Shiny app. The\ncontent of the app reflects the annotations present in the\npassed GuideSet object, and includes intuitive tools to\nexamine, filter, and export gRNAs, thereby making gRNA design\nmore user-friendly.
#> 420                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The cBioPortalData R package accesses study datasets from\nthe cBio Cancer Genomics Portal. It accesses the data either\nfrom the pre-packaged zip / tar files or from the API interface\nthat was recently implemented by the cBioPortal Data Team. The\npackage can provide data in either tabular format or with\nMultiAssayExperiment object that uses familiar Bioconductor\ndata representations.
#> 421                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        SingleMoleculeFootprinting provides functions to analyze\nSingle Molecule Footprinting (SMF) data. Following the workflow\nexemplified in its vignette, the user will be able to perform\nbasic data analysis of SMF data with minimal coding effort.\nStarting from an aligned bam file, we show how to perform\nquality controls over sequencing libraries, extract methylation\ninformation at the single molecule level accounting for the two\npossible kind of SMF experiments (single enzyme or double\nenzyme), classify single molecules based on their patterns of\nmolecular occupancy, plot SMF information at a given genomic\nlocation.
#> 422                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         An R implementation of the correlation-based method\ndeveloped in the Joshi laboratory to analyse and filter\nprocessed single-cell RNAseq data. It returns a filtered\nversion of the data containing only genes expression values\nunaffected by systematic noise.
#> 423                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             seqsetvis enables the visualization and analysis of sets\nof genomic sites in next gen sequencing data. Although\nseqsetvis was designed for the comparison of mulitple ChIP-seq\nsamples, this package is domain-agnostic and allows the\nprocessing of multiple genomic coordinate files (bed-like\nfiles) and signal files (bigwig files pileups from bam file).\nseqsetvis has multiple functions for fetching data from regions\ninto a tidy format for analysis in data.table or tidyverse and\nvisualization via ggplot2.
#> 424                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            SpaceTrooper performs Quality Control analysis using data\ndriven GLM models of Image-Based spatial data, providing\nexploration plots, QC metrics computation, outlier detection.\nIt implements a GLM strategy for the detection of low quality\ncells in imaging-based spatial data (Transcriptomics and\nProteomics). It additionally implements several plots for the\nvisualization of imaging based polygons through the ggplot2\npackage.
#> 425                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         In high resolution mass spectrometry (HR-MS), the measured\nmasses can be decomposed into potential element combinations\n(chemical sum formulas). Where additional mass/intensity\ninformation of respective isotopic peaks is available,\ndecomposition can take this information into account to better\nrank the potential candidate sum formulas. To compare measured\nmass/intensity information with the theoretical distribution of\ncandidate sum formulas, the latter needs to be calculated. This\npackage implements fast algorithms to address both tasks, the\ncalculation of isotopic distributions for arbitrary sum\nformulas (assuming a HR-MS resolution of roughly 30,000), and\nthe ranked list of sum formulas fitting an observed peak or\nisotopic peak set.
#> 426                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 TreeAndLeaf implements a hybrid layout strategy that\nenhances leaf-level visualization in dendrograms. By\nintegrating force-directed graph and tree layout algorithms, it\nenables projection of multiple layers of information onto\ngraph–tree diagrams.
#> 427                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     RedeR combines an R package with a stand-alone Java\napplication for interactive visualization and manipulation of\nnested networks. Graph, node, and edge attributes can be\nconfigured using either graphical or command-line methods,\nfollowing igraph syntax rules.
#> 428                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             MIRit is an R package that provides several methods for\ninvestigating the relationships between miRNAs and genes in\ndifferent biological conditions. In particular, MIRit allows to\nexplore the functions of dysregulated miRNAs, and makes it\npossible to identify miRNA-gene regulatory axes that control\nbiological pathways, thus enabling the users to unveil the\ncomplexity of miRNA biology. MIRit is an all-in-one framework\nthat aims to help researchers in all the central aspects of an\nintegrative miRNA-mRNA analyses, from differential expression\nanalysis to network characterization.
#> 429                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    BreastSubtypeR provides an assumption-aware, multi-method\nframework for intrinsic molecular subtyping of breast cancer.\nThe package harmonizes several published nearest-centroid (NC)\nand single-sample predictor (SSP) classifiers, supplies\nmethod-specific preprocessing and robust probe-to-gene mapping,\nand implements a cohort-aware AUTO mode that selectively\nenables classifiers compatible with the cohort composition. A\nlocal Shiny app (iBreastSubtypeR) is included for interactive\nanalyses and to support users without programming experience.
#> 430                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Uses platform-specific implemenations of the GatingML2.0\nstandard to exchange gated cytometry data with other software\nplatforms.
#> 431                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This package estimates tumor purity, copy number, and loss\nof heterozygosity (LOH), and classifies single nucleotide\nvariants (SNVs) by somatic status and clonality. PureCN is\ndesigned for targeted short read sequencing data, integrates\nwell with standard somatic variant detection and copy number\npipelines, and has support for tumor samples without matching\nnormal samples.
#> 432                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Fit a latent embedding multivariate regression (LEMUR)\nmodel to multi-condition single-cell data. The model provides a\nparametric description of single-cell data measured with\ntreatment vs. control or more complex experimental designs. The\nparametric model is used to (1) align conditions, (2) predict\nlog fold changes between conditions for all cells, and (3)\nidentify cell neighborhoods with consistent log fold changes.\nFor those neighborhoods, a pseudobulked differential expression\ntest is conducted to assess which genes are significantly\nchanged.
#> 433                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        svaRetro contains functions for detecting retrotransposed\ntranscripts (RTs) from structural variant calls. It takes\nstructural variant calls in GRanges of breakend notation and\nidentifies RTs by exon-exon junctions and insertion sites. The\ncandidate RTs are reported by events and annotated with\ninformation of the inserted transcripts.
#> 434                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Implements a variety of methods for combining p-values in\ndifferential analyses of genome-scale datasets. Functions can\ncombine p-values across different tests in the same analysis\n(e.g., genomic windows in ChIP-seq, exons in RNA-seq) or for\ncorresponding tests across separate analyses (e.g., replicated\ncomparisons, effect of different treatment conditions). Support\nis provided for handling log-transformed input p-values,\nmissing values and weighting where appropriate.
#> 435                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  RTNsurvival integrates regulons inferred by the RTN\npackage with survival data. For each regulon, a two-tailed GSEA\nframework computes a differential Enrichment Score (dES) at the\nindividual-sample level. The resulting dES distribution across\nsamples is then used to evaluate survival associations within\nthe cohort. Two primary workflows are supported: (i) Cox\nproportional hazards models, in which regulon activities are\ntreated as predictors of survival time, and (ii) Kaplan–Meier\nanalyses assessing cohort stratification based on regulon\nactivity. All graphical outputs are customizable according to\nuser specifications.
#> 436                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        RTNduals identifies co-regulatory loops between pairs of\nregulons inferred by the RTN package by evaluating their shared\ntarget genes. It infers dual regulons and tests whether\nregulator pairs exhibit cooperative or competitive influences\non common targets.

#> 13                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Version 1.1.1: statistical correctness fixes, new tests, worked examples\n\n- Fix bug within component 2/3 likelihood.\n- Fix bug ZIP/ZINB zero formula\n- Rewrite Neighbours_combined with neighbour counting efficient\n- ABC step uses proposed gamma and correctly-scaled epsilon efficiently\n- Remove proposal density from MH ratio\n\n- compute_HMRFHiC_probabilities: max_interactions defaults to NA (no cap)\n- compute_HMRFHiC_probabilities: new consistent_dist argument (default TRUE)\n- process_data: user now specify rescales or zero-pads easily\n- run_chain_betas: per-dataset x_vars subsetting; Windows mc_cores warning\n\n- Remove duplicate R implementations of C++-backed functions\n- Added more comprehensive test suite\n- Added worked examples vignette section for Hi-C and Micro-C\n

               Removed mkl dependency for mac support and removed .bbsoptions for upcoming R universe build system\n
#> 170                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    block some CHR-dependent unit tests, fix some doc\n
#> 171                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Update downsample logic for scuttle/tatami and fix tests (#129)\n\n* move to non-exact comparison\n\n* Updated downsampling C++ code to use new scuttle functions.\n\nAlso added some more checks to ensure we don't lose integer precision.\n\n* Stripped out test comparisons to downsampleMatrix.\n\nThese tests no longer make sense because the downsampling is no longer done on\na per-event basis (i.e. single UMIs or reads in each count). Rather, the new\nalgorithm operates on the entire count at once, for greater efficiency.\n\nThis all means that UMI and read counts are no longer interchangeable, which\nmeans that the results from downsampleReads/Matrix are no longer directly\ncomparable. This is okay - the test itself was highly contrived anyway as it\nonly works when every UMI has a single read.\n\n* Bumped version and date, updated NEWS.\n\n---------\n\nCo-authored-by: LTLA <infinite.monkeys.with.keyboards@gmail.com>

#> 433                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Fix gene symbol lookup for Ensembl transcript IDs in newer TxDb\n\nRoot cause: TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene now uses Ensembl transcript IDs\n(ENST...) instead of UCSC IDs (uc...). The static gene_symbol.txt lookup table\nonly mapped UCSC kgIDs to gene symbols, so all gene symbols resolved to NA.\n\nFix:\n- Update .txs2genesym() to handle both UCSC and Ensembl transcript IDs\n  - First tries static UCSC lookup table (backward compatible)\n  - Falls back to dynamic TxDb + org.Hs.eg.db lookup for Ensembl IDs\n- Pass genes TxDb to .txs2genesym() from eventDetection.R\n- Add AnnotationDbi to Imports, org.Hs.eg.db to Suggests\n- Replace dplyr::as_tibble with as.data.frame for Hits objects\n- Clean up vignette diagnostic code\n- Bump version to 1.17.5\n
